Customer to share production traffic profile and key prompts (Ethan) by 2026-12-14

Liam Ortega - draft benchmark plan and test script, include KV cache + batching runs - due 2026-12-17

header:
Date: 2026-12-10
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Aria Patel (Redwood CSM); Priya Rao (NovaSense CTO), Ethan Park (ML Eng), Carlos Mendes (Platform Eng), Sofia Alvarez (PM), Zoe Kim (SRE)
summary: Quarterly health + pilot planning: prioritized runway for model rollouts, capacity sizing options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), initial pilot scope and benchmarks, security/gov checklist. Agreed next steps for pricing, benchmark runbook, and data artifacts.
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we know it's a busy week so we'll run through the health snapshot then get into pilot scope.
00:14 Priya Rao: Thanks Maya, yeah we've got a full team here, wanted to make sure we align on capacity because the holiday feature drop is next quarter; some of the numbers from our side changed.
00:29 Liam Ortega: Quick note, I'll run through the perf tradeoffs — for example when you move from hosted to dedicated you see predictable p99s but you pay more for baseline. Also we can do cluster autoscale with burst to cover spiky traffic.
00:45 Ethan Park: Right, our peak is brief — 2x baseline for 10-15 min windows. Most calls are short chat completions, about 120 tokens on average, but we have a set of heavy prompts where sequence length goes to 1k.
01:05 Carlos Mendes: And platform constraint: we have a strict VPC egress rule, so private deployment is preferable if it reduces egress auditing. We are also evaluating KMS integration for keys.
01:20 Maya Chen: Understood. For pilot we usually recommend a staged approach: start with hosted to validate correctness and then move to dedicated or private for SLA-critical paths. We can pin model versions and use automatic fallback to smaller model when capacity is constrained.
01:38 Sofia Alvarez: What's the difference in pricing for a canary on hosted vs one on dedicated — like rough order of magnitude?
01:45 Maya Chen: Short answer: hosted is lowest friction and lower up-front, dedicated has reservation/commit cost but unit cost per token is lower at scale. We'll send a tailored matrix, but think of dedicated as better if you need predictable throughput for millions of calls.
02:05 Zoe Kim: Also SOC 2 scope — do you provide audit logs for private deployments?
02:12 Aria Patel: Yes, we include audit logs and you can push to your logging stack; for private we can integrate with your SSO and KMS/HSM for key management. I'll attach the security checklist after.
02:28 Priya Rao: Can you run through the benchmark plan? We want to see p50/p95/p99 with and without KV cache enabled.
02:36 Liam Ortega: Sure — plan is: we run synthetic traffic that mirrors your 24-hour distribution, run three passes: cold-start (no cache), warmed KV cache, and continuous batching enabled. We'll measure latency distribution, GPU utilization, and cost-per-1k tokens. We'll also test sequence length variance to see kernel selection impact.
03:05 Ethan Park: Any chance you can run that in our staging VPC? We want to ensure network flakiness is represented.
03:12 Liam Ortega: Yes, we can run in VPC peered staging environment; that will show realistic egress/latency. We'll need IAM role and a small sample of anonymized prompts.
03:25 Priya Rao: We'll produce the prompts but want to be careful about PII — we'll redact as needed.
03:32 Maya Chen: Totally, send the redacted set. Also can you include your SLA expectations? We heard p99 of 600ms for 120-token requests as a target, is that still right?
03:45 Priya Rao: That's correct for interactive features. For batch scoring, latency can be more relaxed.
03:52 Carlos Mendes: One risk for us is cold-start spikes after a deploy. Do you have a recommended rollout with graceful degradation?
04:00 Liam Ortega: Yes, we suggest canary deploys with traffic shaping and automatic fallback to a lighter model or a queued mode. Redwood's runtime supports KV cache rehydration and continuous batching to smooth that.
04:20 Ethan Park: What about quantized model quality — we rely on top-k safety filters and semantic fidelity matters. If we quantize, will hallucination rates change?
04:30 Maya Chen: Good question — quantization can sometimes change token probabilities slightly. We recommend running the eval harness during the pilot to compare outputs against your golden prompts. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles with validation metrics.
04:50 Sofia Alvarez: Timeline — we wanted a pilot that validates both perf and output quality before end of January. Is that feasible?
04:58 Liam Ortega: Yes, if we get artifacts by mid-December we can run a bench and a quality sweep in the last two weeks of December and then a short production pilot in January. So target: artifacts by 2026-12-14, bench by 2026-12-20, pilot kickoff early Jan.
05:25 Priya Rao: Are there any gotchas on data residency? We need EU proof if we route EU traffic.
05:32 Maya Chen: We can route by region and pin instances to EU regions; for private deployments you can host on-prem or in your cloud region for residency requirements.
05:45 Carlos Mendes: On monitoring — we need token-level cost breakout and per-route latency dashboards.
05:52 Aria Patel: That's available in the Redwood Console; we'll share a demo link and a 14-day retention sample. We can also export to your Grafana via tracing hooks.
06:08 Ethan Park: A minor transcription note: we sometimes call the runtime 'Redwood Node' internally, is that the same as 'serving runtime'?
06:15 Liam Ortega: Yeah, folks use different names. The serving runtime is the infra component that schedules kernels, manages KV caches, and does batching — sometimes we call it the Node or inference engine.
06:30 Priya Rao: What about fallback policy if dedicated pool reaches capacity? We need hard SLAs and fallback to hosted or smaller model, but with preserved correctness.
06:40 Maya Chen: We can configure routing policies: prefer dedicated, fallback to hosted compatible variants, and use model variants that preserve API shape. We'll configure A/B rollout and automatic rollbacks on regressions.
06:58 Sofia Alvarez: Any compliance docs we should review?
07:02 Aria Patel: I'll attach SOC 2 summary, ISO certs, data processing addendum, and the private deployment checklist. Expect that in email after this call.
07:15 Priya Rao: Sounds good. For the pilot success criteria, can we write metrics: p95 < 350ms for 120-token, hallucination delta < 2% on golden prompts, throughput >= 2k qps sustained for 10 minutes?
07:31 Maya Chen: That's reasonable; we'll map those into the pilot runbook. We may propose different thresholds for EU region routing depending on instance sizing.
07:44 Ethan Park: One more on cost modeling: can you show a baseline unit cost for hosted and an amortized cost for reserved GPUs at 70% utilization?
07:55 Liam Ortega: Yes we'll include cost-per-1M tokens and amortized GPU monthly cost examples in the pricing matrix. Also show break-even point by token volume.
08:12 Priya Rao: Any references to competitors and how you differ on reliability?
08:18 Maya Chen: Short take: we focus on observability and predictable economics, transparent unit pricing, model-versioning and rollouts, and the fallbacks; some vendors only offer hosted endpoints without private options or capacity guarantees.
08:35 Carlos Mendes: For the benchmarking, include a stress run that simulates a deploy during peak traffic to see degradation behavior.
08:43 Liam Ortega: We'll do that — simulated deploy + traffic spike to measure recovery and fallback.
08:57 Sofia Alvarez: OK, recap please?
09:00 Maya Chen: Recap: 1) NovaSense to share anonymized prompts and traffic profile by 12/14 (Ethan). 2) Redwood will send pilot pricing matrix and dedicated SKUs by 12/15 (Maya). 3) Redwood SE will deliver benchmark plan and run in staging VPC week of 12/20 (Liam). 4) Aria will share compliance pack and success criteria doc by 12/13. 5) Next call: bench results review — propose 2026-12-22.
09:28 Priya Rao: That works. Thanks everyone.
09:32 Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with links: benchmark sheet (link: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/NS-2026), security checklist (link: https://redwood.docs/sec/ns-checklist), pricing matrix attachment.
09:50 Meeting end
notes: Shared artifacts: benchmark sheet (link), security checklist (link), sample pricing matrix (attachment)
Proposed pilot window: late Dec bench, early Jan pilot
